en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.14.
Parittārammaṇattika (The Triplet on Limited Objects)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent on a state with a limited object, a state with a limited object arises by way of root condition—[namely] a state with a limited object...

Dependent on one aggregate with a limited object, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with a limited object, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates.
Dependent on a state with a sublime object, a state with a sublime object arises by way of root condition—[dependent on] a state with a sublime object.
Dependent on one aggregate with a sublime object, three aggregates [arise] ... two aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking, [dependent on aggregates] having a sublime object ... [etc. ...

Dependent on a state with an immeasurable object, a state with an immeasurable object arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate with an immeasurable object, three aggregates [arise] ... two aggregates. Object condition, etc.
Dependent on a state with limited object, a state with limited object arises by way of object-condition … by way of predominance-condition (abbreviated) … by way of non-disappearance-condition.
Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.
In the cause condition, three; in the object condition, three; in the predominance condition, three …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, three. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive. 1.14.1.2.
Negative Conditionality.
Section on Analysis:
Not-root Condition. Dependent on a state with limited object, a state with limited object arises by way of the not-root condition—that is, a rootless [state].

Dependent on one aggregate with a limited object, there arise three aggregates … two aggregates. At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with a limited object, there arise three aggregates … two aggregates;
and dependent on the doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates, there arises doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion.
Dependent on a state with a sublime object, a state with a sublime object arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate with a sublime object, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates;
dependent on the doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates, doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion arises.

Dependent on a state with an immeasurable object, a state with an immeasurable object arises by way of the not-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate with an immeasurable object, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates.

Not-predominance Condition (*na-adhipati-paccaya*): Dependent on a state with a limited object, a state with a limited object arises by way of the not-predominance condition: dependent on one aggregate with a limited object, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking … etc.

Dependent on a state with a sublime object (mahaggatārammaṇa), a state with a sublime object arises by way of the not-predominance condition (na-adhipati-paccaya): dependent on one aggregate with a sublime object, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state with an immeasurable object (appamāṇārammaṇa), a state with an immeasurable object arises by way of the not-predominance condition: dependent on one aggregate with an immeasurable object, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates. [This concludes the section on] Not-Prenascence and the others.

Dependent on a state with limited object, a state with limited object arises by way of not-prenascence condition: in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with limited object, three aggregates arise … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….
Dependent on a state with exalted object, a state with exalted object arises by way of not-prenascence condition:
in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with exalted object, three aggregates arise … pe … two aggregates. (There is no rebirth-linking with exalted objects.)
Dependent on a state with an immeasurable object, a state with an immeasurable object arises by way of not-prenascence condition:
in the formless realm, dependent on one aggregate with an immeasurable object, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates.
(The not-postnascence condition and the not-repetition condition are similar to the not-predominance condition.)
Dependent on a state with a limited object, a state with a limited object arises by way of non-kamma condition: dependent on aggregates with a limited object, volition with a limited object arises.
Dependent on a state with a sublime object, a state with a sublime object arises by way of non-kamma condition: dependent on aggregates with a sublime object, volition with a sublime object arises.

Dependent on a state with an immeasurable object, a state with an immeasurable object arises by way of not-kamma condition: dependent on aggregates with an immeasurable object, volition with an immeasurable object [arises].
Not-resultant, etc.:
Dependent on a state with a limited object, a state with a limited object arises by way of not-resultant condition (*na-vipāka-paccaya*) [at rebirth-linking...]
… [There is] no jhāna condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by the fivefold sense-consciousness, there arise three aggregates … two aggregates … No path condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate with a limited object, there arise three aggregates … two aggregates;
at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … two aggregates … [and so on].

Dependent on a state with a sublime object, a state with a sublime object arises by way of not-path condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate with a sublime object, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates.

Dependent on a state with an immeasurable object, a state with an immeasurable object arises by way of not-path condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate with an immeasurable object, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates.
Not-dissociation.

Dependent on a state with limited object, a state with limited object arises by way of non-dissociation condition: in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with limited object, three aggregates [arise] ... and so forth.

Dependent on a state with exalted object, a state with exalted object arises by way of non-dissociation condition: in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with exalted object, three aggregates [arise] ... and so forth.

Dependent on a state with immeasurable object, a state with immeasurable object arises by way of non-dissociation condition: in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with immeasurable object, three aggregates [arise] ... [and so on] ... two aggregates.
Section on Enumeration:
Pure.
With not-root: three; with not-predominance: three ... pe ... with not-prenascence: three, with not-postnascence: three, with not-repetition:
three, with not-kamma: three, with not-resultant: three, with not-jhāna: one, with not-path: three, with not-dissociation: three. (Enumerate thus. Negative.

1.14.1.3. Positive-Negative Conditionality (Paccayānulomapaccanīya) With root condition (hetupaccaya), there are three [results] for non-predominance (na-adhipati), three for not-prenascence (na-purejāta), three for not-postnascence (na-pacchājāta), three for not-repetition (na-āsevana), three for not-kamma (na-kamma), three for not-resultant (na-vipāka), and three for not-dissociation (na-vippayutta). (Enumerate in this manner.
This concludes the Positive-Negative Conditionality.
1.14.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Conditions (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma): The Non-root Pair (Nahetuduka).

With the non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there are three [results] in the object condition (ārammaṇa), three in the proximity condition (anantara), three in the contiguity condition (samanantara), three in the conascence condition (sahajāta), and [three] in the mutuality condition (aññamañña).
Three for root-cause, three for support, three for decisive support, three for pre-existence, two for repetition, three for kamma, one for result,
three for nutriment, three for faculty, three for jhāna, two for path, three for association, three for dissociation, three for presence, three for absence,
three for disappearance, and three for non-disappearance. (Thus it should be counted.)
Negative-Positive (Paccanīyānuloma).
The Chapter on Dependence (Paṭiccavāra). 1.14.2–6. The Section on Co-nascence Condition, Support, Conjoined, and Associated (Sahajāta-paccaya-nissaya-saṁsaṭṭha-sampayuttavāra).
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, support, association, and conjunction are similar to the section on dependence. 1.14.7.
Chapter of Questions 1.14.7.1.
Positive Conditionality (Paccayānuloma)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition. A state with a limited object is a condition, by way of root condition, for a state with a limited object—namely, those states with a limited object.

Roots with limited objects are related to their associated aggregates by way of root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots with limited objects are related to their associated aggregates by way of root condition.

A state with exalted object is related to a state with exalted object by way of root condition: roots with exalted objects are related to their associated aggregates by way of root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … [same as above].

A state with an immeasurable object is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state with an immeasurable object: roots with immeasurable objects are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates.
Object Condition:
A state with a limited object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a limited object: [the thought of] giving...
Having given a gift, undertaken precepts, and performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews that; one reviews former good deeds;
the Noble Ones review defilements abandoned with respect to a limited object, review defilements suppressed, and know defilements formerly practiced.
[They contemplate] limited aggregates with a limited object as impermanent and as suffering...
One contemplates [it] as non-self; one relishes it and delights in it. Taking that as an object, lust with a limited object arises …pe… mental grief arises.
By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a limited mind with a limited object.
Limited aggregates with a limited object are the objects of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds and the knowledge of recollection of past lives.
Knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their kamma, knowledge of the future, and advertence are related to [their respective objects] by way of object-condition.
A state with a limited object is related to a state with a sublime object by way of object-condition:
one reviews the divine eye, one reviews the divine ear-element, or one reviews the knowledge of the modes of psychic power (iddhividhañāṇa) having a limited object.

He reviews the knowledge of penetration into others' minds …pe… the knowledge of recollection of past lives …pe… the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds …pe… he reviews the knowledge of future existences.
He practices insight into the sublime aggregates with limited objects as impermanent …pe… he enjoys them and delights in them; taking these as an object, lust with a sublime object arises …pe…
Mental grief arises. By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a sublime state of consciousness that has a limited object.

Sublime aggregates with a limited object are related to the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of future existences, and to advertence by way of object-condition.
A state with a sublime object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a sublime object:
one reviews the base of infinite consciousness; one reviews the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; one reviews supernormal power-knowledge (iddhividha-ñāṇa) with a sublime object;

[one reviews] knowledge of the minds of others (cetopariya-ñāṇa) …pe… knowledge of recollection of past lives (pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa) …pe… knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds (yathākammūpaga-ñāṇa).
... pe ... one reviews the knowledge of the future. One contemplates with insight the exalted aggregates, which have an exalted object, as impermanent ...
pe ... one relishes them and delights in them; taking those as an object, lust with an exalted object arises ...
pe ... mental grief arises. By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, [one knows] the mind of one possessing a mind that is exalted and has an exalted object.

[One] knows. Lofty objects are related to lofty aggregates by way of object-condition for the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the destiny according to deeds, the knowledge of future existences, and for advertence.
A state with a lofty object is related to a state with a limited object by way of object-condition—the review of the first jhāna.
He reviews... [as before] ...he reviews the reviewing of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
he reviews the reviewing of the divine eye; he reviews the reviewing of the divine ear-element; he reviews the reviewing of the knowledge of the various supernormal powers...
[as before] ...the reviewing of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds... [as before] ...the reviewing of the knowledge of recollection of past lives... [as before].
...the reviewing of the knowledge of the passing away according to deeds (*yathākammūpagañāṇa*) ...pe... the reviewing of the knowledge of future existences (*anāgataṃsañāṇa*).
Noble ones review defilements that have been abandoned with a sublime object; they review defilements that have been suppressed;
they know defilements formerly practiced. They [review] limited aggregates with a sublime object as impermanent ...pe...
One contemplates it, relishes it, and delights in it; with that as its object, lust with a limited object arises …pe… grief arises.
By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a limited mind that has a sublime object.

Limited aggregates with a sublime object are the object of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of rebirth according to karma.
Knowledge of the future is related to adverting by way of object condition.
A state with an immeasurable object is related to a state with an immeasurable object by way of object condition:
noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path; they review the fruit. By means of knowledge of others' minds...
One knows the consciousness of one possessing immeasurable consciousness with an immeasurable object.

Immeasurable aggregates with immeasurable objects are related to knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of recollection of past lives, knowledge of future existences, and advertence by way of object-condition.
An immeasurable state with an immeasurable object is related to a state with a limited object by way of object-condition—the Noble Ones...
They review the change-of-lineage; they review purification; they review the reviewing of the path;
they review the reviewing of the fruit; they review the reviewing of Nibbāna.

They practice insight into the limited aggregates with an immeasurable object as impermanent ... [and so on] ... By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, [they know] one possessing a limited mind with an immeasurable object.

It knows the mind. Limited aggregates with immeasurable objects are related to knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of recollection of past lives, knowledge of the destination according to deeds, and advertence of knowledge of future existences by way of object-condition.
A state with immeasurable object is related to a state with sublime object by way of object-condition—the Noble Ones...
They review the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds that has an immeasurable object; they review the knowledge of recollection of past lives;
they review the knowledge of future states. By means of the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds, they know the mind of one possessing a sublime mind with an immeasurable object.
The sublime aggregates with an immeasurable object [constitute] the object of the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds and the knowledge of recollection of past lives.
Knowledge of the future is related to advertence by way of object-condition.
Dominance:
A state with a limited object is related to a state with a limited object by way of dominance-condition—namely, objective dominance (ārammaṇādhipati).
Co-nascent predominance. Object-predominance: having given a gift, undertaken virtue, or performed an observance-day duty, one esteems and reviews it; one esteems and reviews past deeds well done;
one esteems, relishes, and delights in limited aggregates that have limited objects; esteeming them, [there arises] that which has a limited object.
Lust arises; a view arises. Co-nascent predominance: a limited object-predominance is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates.
A state with a limited object is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state with a sublime object. Object-predominance: the divine...

Having made the eye an object of esteem, one reviews it; the divine ear-element … [and so on] … the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power with a limited object … [and so on] … the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds … [and so on] … the knowledge of recollection of past lives … [and so on] … the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds … [and so on] … having made the knowledge of future existences an object of esteem, one reviews it.
Having made sublime aggregates with a limited object an object of esteem, one relishes them.
One rejoices; taking that as an object of esteem (*garuṃ katvā*), lust with a sublime object (*mahaggatārammaṇa*) arises, and wrong view arises.

A state with a sublime object is a condition for a state with a sublime object by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*): namely, objective predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*). Objective predominance:
one reviews the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*) taking it as an object of esteem; [one reviews] the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*)...

...pe... one esteems and reviews the knowledge of the various supernormal powers having a lofty object; ...pe... the knowledge of penetration into others' minds; ...pe... the knowledge of recollection of past lives; ...pe...
the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds; ...pe... one esteems and reviews the knowledge of future existences.
Esteeming and delighting in the lofty aggregates that have a lofty object, one esteems them; esteeming them, [there arises] [craving] having a lofty object.
Lust arises; a view arises. Co-nascent predominance: a predominance with a sublime object is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates.
A state with a sublime object is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state with a limited object. Object-predominance: the reviewing of the first jhāna...
One esteems and reviews [them]... one esteems and reviews the reviewing of knowledge of the future.
Esteeming limited aggregates with a lofty object, one relishes them and delights in them;
esteeming them, lust with a limited object arises, and wrong view arises.
A state with an immeasurable object is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state with an immeasurable object:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: Noble ones, having emerged from the Path, esteem and review the Path;
they esteem and review the Fruit. Conascence-predominance: Predominance with an immeasurable object [is a condition] for its associated states...
[This] is a condition for the aggregates by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

A state having an immeasurable object (*appamāṇārammaṇa*) is a condition for a state having a limited object (*parittārammaṇa*) by way of predominance-condition. Object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*):

Learners (*sekkhā*), esteeming it as weighty, reflect upon the change-of-lineage (*gotrabhu*); they esteem it as weighty, reflect upon purification (*vodāna*); [they reflect upon] the reflection on the path (*maggapaccavekkhaṇa*).
They reflect, making it an object of esteem; they reflect, making the reflection on the fruit an object of esteem; they reflect, making the reflection on Nibbāna an object of esteem.
A state with an immeasurable object is related to a state with a sublime object by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Object-predominance: trainees...
They reflect upon the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, making it an object of esteem, as having an immeasurable object. They reflect upon the knowledge of recollection of past lives...
[and so on] ...the knowledge of future states, making them objects of esteem.
Immediately after...
A state with limited object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a state with limited object:
preceding aggregates with limited objects are a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for subsequent aggregates with limited objects.

A state with a limited object (parittārammaṇa) is a condition for a state with a sublime object (mahaggatārammaṇa) by way of proximity condition (anantarapaccaya)—the death-consciousness with a limited object is a condition for the rebirth-consciousness with a sublime object by way of proximity condition;
the life-continuum (bhavaṅga) with a limited object is a condition for the adverting consciousness with a sublime object by way of proximity condition. [States] with a limited object...
The aggregates are related to emergence having a sublime object by way of proximity condition.
A state with a limited object is related to a state with an immeasurable object by way of proximity condition:
the life-continuum (bhavaṅga) with a limited object is related to advertence (āvajjanā) with an immeasurable object by way of proximity condition. [A state] with a limited object...
Adaptation is related to change-of-lineage, adaptation is related to purification, and adaptation is related to the attainment of fruition by way of proximity condition.
A state with exalted object is related to a state with exalted object by way of proximity condition:
preceding aggregates with exalted objects are related to subsequent aggregates with exalted objects.
Condition by way of proximity condition.
A state having a sublime object is a condition for a state having a limited object by way of proximity condition:
a death-consciousness with a sublime object is a condition for a rebirth-consciousness with a limited object by way of proximity condition. [A state] having a sublime object...
The life-continuum (bhavaṅga) is related to an advertence (āvajjanā) having a limited object by way of proximity-condition (anantara-paccaya).
Aggregates having a sublime object are related to emergence (vuṭṭhāna) having a limited object by way of proximity-condition.
A state having a sublime object is related to a state having an immeasurable object by way of proximity-condition—[namely,] a [state] having a sublime object...
The life-continuum (bhavaṅga) is related to the adverting consciousness with an immeasurable object by way of proximity condition.

A lofty-object conformity (anuloma) is related to the change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) ... conformity is related to purification (vodāna) ... conformity is related to the attainment of fruition (phalasamāpatti).
For one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related to the attainment of fruition by way of proximity condition.
A state with an immeasurable object is a condition for a state with an immeasurable object by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*):
preceding aggregates with immeasurable objects are a condition for subsequent aggregates with immeasurable objects by way of proximity-condition.
Change-of-lineage is a condition for the Path; purification is a condition for the Path; the Path is a condition for the Fruit.
… a fruit is a condition for a fruit by way of proximity-condition.
A state having an immeasurable object is a condition for a state having a limited object by way of proximity-condition—the review of the path is a condition for emergence having a limited object;
… the review of the fruit is a condition for emergence having a limited object.

… the reviewing of Nibbāna is the emergence from that which has a limited object; the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds has an immeasurable object [but is] the emergence from that which has a limited object;
the knowledge of recollection of past lives is the emergence from that which has a limited object;
the knowledge of future existences is the emergence from that which has a limited object; the fruit is the emergence from that which has a limited object.
A state with an immeasurable object is related to a state with a sublime object by way of proximity condition.
Reviewing of the Path is related to emergence with a sublime object; reviewing of the Fruit is related to emergence with a sublime object.
… the reviewing of Nibbāna is related to emergence with a sublime object by way of proximity condition (*anantarapaccaya*).
Immediate succession (*samanantara*)…
A state with a limited object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a state with a limited object. (This is the same as the section on immediate succession. Co-nascent, etc.:

A state with a limited object is a condition, by way of co-nascence-condition, for a state with a limited object; ... by way of mutuality-condition, for a state with a limited object; ... by way of dependence-condition, for a state with a limited object—three [answers]. (These should be made in accordance with the "Dependent" Chapter.)

A state with a limited object is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for a state with a limited object: as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support … [and so on] … Natural decisive support:
faith with a limited object … [and so on] … Natural decisive support: faith with a limited object … [and so on] … Natural decisive support: faith with a limited object.
Depending on [a limited object], one gives a gift; [observes] virtue … [performs] the Uposatha duty … [produces] jhāna with a limited object;
produces insight … [produces] direct knowledge … [produces] attainment; arouses conceit; adopts wrong view.
[One also develops] virtue with a limited object … wisdom … lust … hatred … delusion … conceit … wrong view … aspiration.
… bodily pleasure … depending on bodily pain, one gives a gift, observes virtue … [and so on] … performs the Uposatha duty … [and so on] … arouses jhāna with a limited object,
arouses insight … [and so on] … arouses direct knowledge … [and so on] … arouses attainment,
kills a living being … [and so on] … causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Limited-object faith … [and so on] … wisdom, lust … [and so on] … aspiration.

Bodily pleasure … bodily pain … limited-object faith … pe … wisdom, lust … pe … aspiration, are related to bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and limited-object faith … pe … wisdom, lust … pe … aspiration by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state with a limited object is related to a state with a sublime object by way of decisive support condition— namely, as an object-decisive-support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-prenascence condition, natural-prenascence condition … [and so on] … Natural-prenascence condition:
depending on faith with a limited object, one arouses jhāna with a sublime object, arouses insight … [and so on] … higher knowledge … [and so on] … attainment;
one conceives conceit, adopts wrong view. [Depending on] virtue with a limited object … [and so on] … wisdom … lust … [and so on] … [28]
…pe… aspiration … depending on bodily pleasure and bodily pain, one arouses jhāna with a lofty object,
arouses insight …pe… superknowledge …pe… attainment, conceives conceit, and adopts wrong view.
Faith with a limited object …pe… bodily pleasure and bodily pain [are related] to [faith] with a lofty object.
Faith … pe … wisdom is related to lust … pe … to aspiration by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state with a limited object (*parittārammaṇa*) is related to a state with an immeasurable object (*appamāṇārammaṇa*) by way of decisive support condition—namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … pe ….
Natural decisive support: having relied upon faith with a limited object, [one develops] faith with an immeasurable object.
One arouses jhāna; one arouses the path... higher knowledge... attainment.
Relying upon virtue with a limited object... wisdom, lust... bodily pleasure, or bodily pain, one arouses jhāna with an immeasurable object;
one arouses the path... higher knowledge... attainment. Faith with a limited object... [and so forth].
Bodily pleasure and bodily pain are related to faith and wisdom having an immeasurable object by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state with a sublime object is related to a state with a sublime object by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: faith having a sublime object... [and so forth].
Depending on [a state] with a sublime object, one arouses jhāna, develops insight, develops direct knowledge, or develops attainment;
one arouses conceit or adopts a wrong view. Depending on virtue with a sublime object … pe … wisdom, lust … pe … or aspiration, one arouses jhāna with a sublime object … pe … or adopts a wrong view.
Faith with a sublime object … pe … wisdom; lust … pe … aspiration is related to faith with a sublime object … pe … aspiration by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state with a sublime object is related to a state with a limited object by way of decisive support condition—namely, as object-decisive-support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence … [and so on] … Natural strong-dependence:
depending on faith that has a sublime object, one gives a gift, undertakes precepts, performs the Uposatha duty, arouses jhāna with a limited object,
arouses insight, [arouses] direct knowledge, arouses attainment, conceives conceit, or adopts wrong view.
Virtue with a lofty object ... [and so on] ... by depending on aspiration, one gives a gift ... [and so on] ... adopts a wrong view.
Faith with a lofty object ... [and so on] ... aspiration is related to faith with a limited object ... [and so on] ...
to aspiration, to bodily pleasure, and to bodily pain, by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).

A state with a sublime object is a condition for a state with an immeasurable object by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, as proximity-decisive support (anantara-upanissaya) and natural decisive support (pakata-upanissaya)… [etc. …As natural decisive support: relying on faith with a sublime object, one arouses jhāna with an immeasurable object;
one arouses the Path, direct knowledge (abhiññā), or attainment. [Relying on] virtue with a sublime object…
